steps.label: What antibiotics do
steps.margin_note: Definition with both kill and retard, plus the selectivity.

They act on the microbe without harming the
steps.why: An antibiotic attacks something a bacterium has and a human cell does not, which is why it can kill the microbe and leave the patient alone.
common_mistakes: Saying antibiotics kill viruses. They act on BACTERIA and some fungi, not viruses.
Leaving out 'produced by microbes'. That is where antibiotics come from.
steps.memory_tip: Made by microbes, used against microbes.

steps.label: Which diseases they defeated
steps.margin_note: All four diseases, the scale, and the effect on life expectancy.
lines: Antibiotics greatly increased our capacity to
treat deadly diseases such as PLAGUE, WHOOPING
These used to kill MILLIONS all over the globe.
Antibiotics are one of the reasons average human
life expectancy rose sharply in the last century.
steps.why: These four were among the great killers before antibiotics, so naming them measures the size of the change rather than just asserting it.
common_mistakes: Naming no disease. The four named ones are the second mark.
Saying antibiotics eliminated all disease. Resistance is now a serious problem.
steps.memory_tip: Four names that used to mean death.
